name: owamp
desc: Implementation of the One-Way Active Measurement Protocol
why: A door into One-Way Active Measurement Protocol, measuring one-direction latency and packet loss between hosts, an unusual look at network timing.

brief.what_it_is: OWAMP is an implementation of the One-Way Active Measurement Protocol, per the Brew description and the GitHub About line ("A tool for performing one-way or two-way active measurements"). The Brew entry lists seven executables: owampd, owfetch, owping, owstats, owtvec, owup, and powstream. I could not retrieve the README, so I cannot confirm from the project's own text what each one takes in or emits. The homepage is a generic Internet2 Performance Tools page that does not describe OWAMP specifically.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames the wider toolkit as tools to "help network engineers quickly identify service problems across national and international networks." I did not find an OWAMP-specific rationale in the pages I could read.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says the wider performance tools are distributed "as both source code and binary packages in the RPM format." The GitHub repo has a Makefile and a .gitmodules file, which suggests a source build with submodules, but I did not read the build instructions. Nothing about hardware, accounts, or first-run configuration was visible.
brief.standout: OWAMP measures each direction of a path separately, so a one-way latency or loss figure does not get blended with the return path. The scout note calls this an unusual look at network timing. I could not confirm the clock or measurement details from the README.
brief.status: Likely maintained, but unverified. The GitHub page showed 1,501 commits, 88 stars, 31 forks, a .github/workflows directory, and an Apache-2.0 license. I could not see a release date or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The homepage is generic and does not mention OWAMP. The README fetch returned 404 on the raw URL, and the repo page returned only the LICENSE text, so the project's own description of usage is missing from these notes. The scout note says one-way measurement, while the repo says one-way or two-way; the writer should check. The Brew entry has no caveats. Platform support and build requirements are unknown.

These dependable tools enable the installation, configuration, and management of performance monitoring software\u2014available as both source code and binary packages in the RPM format.
Performance monitoring tools to help network engineers quickly identify service problems across national and international networks.
